<h1 class="visually-hidden">Noah Buckley</h1>

::: {.hero}
::: {.hero-text}
I am an assistant professor (with tenure) in the [Department of Political Science](https://www.tcd.ie/Political_Science/) at [Trinity College Dublin](https://www.tcd.ie). I received my Ph.D. from Columbia University in 2017 and was previously a postdoctoral associate at NYU Abu Dhabi.

My research is on authoritarian politics, mostly in Putin-era Russia: how autocratic regimes sustain themselves, how ordinary people understand and respond to the political environment they live in, and why corruption persists. I combine large-scale survey data with observational data I build myself from scraped and hand-coded sources, and use it to identify the effects of political events and information on attitudes and behaviour under authoritarianism.

My work has appeared in the *American Political Science Review*, *American Journal of Political Science*, *Comparative Political Studies*, *Comparative Politics*, *Journal of Experimental Political Science*, *Europe-Asia Studies*, and *Post-Soviet Affairs*. A full list is on the [research](research.qmd) page.
